summary: The study reports the synthesis and application of a new highly volatile In(III) triazenide precursor for the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of high-quality epitaxial hexagonal InN. The precursor undergoes gas-phase thermal decomposition at higher temperatures, producing a more reactive In(III) compound while maintaining self-limiting growth behavior. The resulting InN films are stoichiometric with low impurity levels and exhibit good electrical properties, making them suitable for semiconductor applications.
evidence: The new homoleptic triazenide precursor, the first example used in a vapor deposition process, was easily synthesized and thermogravimetric analysis showed single step volatilization with an onset temperature of 145 °C with negligible residual mass. The InN films deposited at 325 °C had a sheet resistivity of 920 Ω2. This new triazenide precursor enables ALD of InN for semiconductor applications and provides a new family of M–N bonded precursors for future deposition processes.
